decisive_items: hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow
thrombus extending into the right atrium
The patient developed hepatorenal syndrome requiring continuous venovenous hemofiltration
response.rationale: Hepatic vein thrombosis with portal flow reversal and secondary hepatorenal syndrome define Budd-Chiari syndrome, whereas the pericardial mass is a downstream thrombus extension rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Describes the imaging finding but is the consequence of venous thrombus extension, not the underlying syndrome.
IVC thrombosis is a component of the extensive thrombotic process, but the hepatic vein thrombosis is the key diagnostic feature.
No evidence of a hepatic mass or chronic liver disease stigmata to support hepatocellular carcinoma.
Tumor thrombus is unsupported; the mass is contiguous with venous thrombus, not a neoplastic primary.
Hepatorenal syndrome is a downstream complication, not the underlying diagnosis.
Lower-extremity thrombosis is part of the hypercoagulable/thrombotic picture but not the most specific diagnosis.
